messages.text:
The duplicate/missing-value handling is patched.

I’m doing one last comparison pass over those parser cases, plus a quick smoke of the runnable command, then I’ll wrap up with what changed and the known timing caveat.

commands.commandLine:
"C:\\Program Files\\PowerShell\\7\\pwsh.exe" -Command "@'
import subprocess,pathlib,sys,json
ref=pathlib.Path('REFERENCE_BINARY.txt').read_text().strip()
cases=[['-i'],['-w'],['-1'],['-i','rust-reference/test-files/2.test.txt.zip','-i','rust-reference/test-files/3.test.txt.zip'],['-i','rust-reference/test-files/2.test.txt.zip','-c','l','-c','d'],['-i','rust-reference/test-files/2.test.txt.zip','--workers','1','--workers','2'],['--foo']]
for args in cases:
 rr=subprocess.run([ref]+args,capture_output=True,text=True,timeout=10)
 pr=subprocess.run([sys.executable,'zip_password_finder.py']+args,capture_output=True,text=True,timeout=10)
 print('CASE',args,'codes',rr.returncode,pr.returncode,'out',rr.stdout==pr.stdout,'err',rr.stderr==pr.stderr)
 if rr.stderr"'!=pr.stderr: print('"'REF',repr(rr.stderr),'PY',repr(pr.stderr))
'@ | python -"
